stories.headline: Samsung posts first-ever 100T-won quarterly profit, lifts 2026 capex 60% as 2027 HBM sells out

key_facts.fact: Samsung Electronics reported Q3 2026 consolidated revenue of KRW 195.3 trillion, an all-time quarterly high up 14% QoQ, and operating profit of KRW 107.4 trillion, making it the world's first tech company to exceed KRW 100 trillion in quarterly operating profit.
key_facts.excerpt: The Company posted KRW 195.3 trillion in consolidated revenue, another all-time quarterly high... Operating profit reached KRW 107.4 trillion, making Samsung Electronics the world's first tech company to exceed KRW 100 trillion in quarterly operating profit.

key_facts.fact: The Device Solutions (chip) division posted KRW 147.1 trillion in revenue and KRW 106.5 trillion in operating profit; the consumer-device DX division recorded an operating loss of KRW 0.8 trillion.
key_facts.excerpt: The DS Division posted KRW 147.1 trillion in consolidated revenue and KRW 106.5 trillion in operating profit... The Device eXperience (DX) Division ... recorded an operating loss of KRW 0.8 trillion.

key_facts.fact: Samsung expects 2026 capital expenditure of about KRW 84.4 trillion (about $63 billion), up more than 60%, including KRW 76.8 trillion for the chip division, with spending on new fabs in Yongin, Gwangju and Taylor, Texas.
key_facts.excerpt: Capital expenditure this year, centered on fab investment, also came in higher than initially expected at 84.4 trillion won, up 60% from last year... with investment accelerating at new fabs in Yongin, Gwangju in Jeolla Province and Taylor, Texas

key_facts.fact: HBM4 revenue more than tripled from the previous quarter to about 60% of Samsung's HBM revenue; 2027 HBM supply volumes have been negotiated and are already sold out, with long-term agreements signed with 10 customers.
key_facts.excerpt: our HBM4 revenue in the third quarter increased more than threefold from the previous quarter, and HBM4's share of our total HBM revenue expanded to around 60%... Negotiations for 2027 supply volumes have been completed at prices in line with our target... and the supply has already been sold out.

key_facts.fact: Samsung's HBM market share rose to the high-30% range in Q3, up from about 20% in Q1, closing in on SK Hynix at about 50%, according to industry accounts.
key_facts.excerpt: Samsung's HBM market share rose to the high 30% range in the third quarter, according to industry accounts. Its share stood at around 20% as recently as the first quarter... within striking distance of SK hynix at about 50%.

key_facts.fact: Chip-division operating income fell about 2% short of estimates and Samsung withheld plans for future shareholder payouts until January, sending its stock lower.
key_facts.excerpt: chip-division operating income fell about 2% shy of estimates and the company withheld plans for future shareholder payouts till January, dashing investors' hopes

stories.headline: Marvell in advanced talks to buy $83 billion optics maker Lumentum, Bloomberg reports

key_facts.fact: Marvell Technology is in advanced talks to buy data center optics maker Lumentum Holdings, and a deal could be announced as soon as next week, people familiar told Bloomberg on October 28.
key_facts.excerpt: Marvell Technology Inc. is in advanced talks to buy data center optics maker Lumentum Holdings Inc.... A transaction may be announced as soon as next week, the people said

key_facts.fact: Nvidia-backed Lumentum has a market value of about $83 billion; Marvell is worth around $221 billion.
key_facts.excerpt: Lumentum, which is backed by Nvidia Corp., has a market value of about $83 billion, while Marvell is worth around $221 billion.

key_facts.fact: Lumentum shares soared 15% in after-hours trading on the report while Marvell dropped 11%.
key_facts.excerpt: Lumentum Holdings (LITE) soared 15% in after-hours trading on a report that Marvell Technology (MRVL) is in advanced discussions to buy the data center optics maker. Marvell dropped 11%.

key_facts.fact: Lumentum makes its own indium phosphide lasers used in Nvidia's Spectrum-X and Quantum-X networking switches, while Marvell is fabless; the deal would dwarf the $3.25 billion Marvell paid for Celestial AI.
key_facts.excerpt: the latter manufactures its own indium phosphide (InP) lasers – which feature in Nvidia's Spectrum-X and Quantum-X networking switches. Where Marvell is fabless, Lumentum is actively building out production capacity amid a dearth of laser supplies

key_facts.fact: Neither Marvell nor Lumentum responded to requests for comment.
key_facts.excerpt: Marvell and Lumentum did not immediately respond to Reuters requests for comment.

stories.headline: NYT: US officials say Megaspeed exec close to Jensen Huang is a Chinese intelligence asset

key_facts.fact: US officials concluded that Alice Huang (Huang Le), a top executive at Singapore-based data center company Megaspeed under scrutiny for possibly steering Nvidia AI chips to China, was a Chinese intelligence asset who developed a close relationship with Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang, the New York Times reported on October 29.
key_facts.excerpt: A top executive at a Singapore-based data center company was under scrutiny for possibly steering advanced Nvidia A.I. chips to China. And now American officials had concluded that she was a Chinese intelligence asset... she had developed a close relationship with Jensen Huang

key_facts.fact: President Trump was briefed on the findings and took no action; per the Times he was concerned about disrupting Nvidia's sales and relations with China.
key_facts.excerpt: President Donald Trump was briefed on the findings about a year ago but chose not to act... Trump was concerned about disrupting Nvidia's sales and complicating relations with China.

key_facts.fact: Megaspeed's Malaysian sister company bought at least $4.8 billion in advanced AI equipment containing Nvidia chips between June 2024 and February 2026, and the Commerce Department's investigation was transferred to the Justice Department this year.
key_facts.excerpt: Megaspeed's Malaysian sister company bought at least $4.8 billion in advanced artificial-intelligence equipment containing Nvidia chips between June 2024 and February 2026... The Times said the Commerce Department's investigation was transferred to the Justice Department this year.

key_facts.fact: Officials do not believe Jensen Huang knew of the alleged activities, and he has not received a defensive briefing; surveillance of Alice Huang continues.
key_facts.excerpt: Mr. Huang hasn't yet been given a defensive briefing... even though the surveillance against Alice Huang continues... U.S. officials do not believe that he is aware of Ms. Huang's intelligence activities.

key_facts.fact: Nvidia said Jensen Huang's interactions with Alice Huang were 'not unusual or unexpected' and that regional cloud customers receive 'zero information relevant to national security'; the Chinese embassy called the allegations 'groundless smears'.
key_facts.excerpt: "Jensen's interactions with Ms. Huang are not unusual or unexpected... Our regional cloud customers receive ordinary business information — not sensitive NVIDIA trade secrets — and zero information relevant to national security."... The Chinese embassy in Washington denied the allegations, saying that it was merely "groundless smears and slanders"

key_facts.fact: Megaspeed said it takes the allegations seriously and has retained outside lawyers for an internal investigation; Nvidia says it has found no evidence of smuggling.
key_facts.excerpt: Megaspeed said it took the allegations seriously and had retained outside lawyers to conduct an internal investigation... Nvidia says it complies with applicable laws and has found no evidence of smuggling.

stories.headline: DOJ questions Nvidia's $12.93B Hugging Face deal as broader antitrust probe of chipmaker continues

key_facts.fact: The US Department of Justice has made inquiries about how Nvidia's $12.93 billion deal to buy open-source AI platform Hugging Face would affect competition, Reuters reported on October 28, citing two people familiar.
key_facts.excerpt: The US Department of Justice has made inquiries about how Nvidia's $12.93 billion deal to buy open-source platform Hugging Face would affect competition in artificial intelligence

key_facts.fact: DOJ officials asked whether the deal would let Nvidia 'capture a fundamental distribution point for AI'; the acquisition is expected to close in the first half of 2027.
key_facts.excerpt: On Hugging Face, Justice Department officials have asked whether the deal would let Nvidia capture a fundamental distribution point for AI, the people said. The acquisition is expected to close in the first half of 2027

key_facts.fact: The DOJ's broader conduct probe, begun under Biden, has examined whether Nvidia offered larger AI chip allocations to customers who bought its networking gear and Groq processors, and has looked at its SchedMD and Run:ai acquisitions.
key_facts.excerpt: Officials have explored whether Nvidia unfairly offered larger allocations of AI chips if customers purchased its networking equipment and Groq processors... The DOJ has also looked at Nvidia's acquisition of Run:ai

key_facts.fact: CNBC confirmed the probe; the Hugging Face deal is Nvidia's second-biggest purchase after the $20 billion it paid for Groq assets at the end of last year.
key_facts.excerpt: The Hugging Face deal marked Nvidia's second-biggest purchase, after it paid $20 billion for Groq assets at the end of last year.

key_facts.fact: A DOJ spokesperson declined to comment, adding that the department 'will continue to prioritize advancement of Super Intelligence for the betterment of the American people'; Nvidia declined to comment.
key_facts.excerpt: "This DOJ under President Trump's leadership will continue to prioritize advancement of Super Intelligence for the betterment of the American people." Nvidia declined to comment

stories.headline: Korean AI chip startup FuriosaAI raises $620M Series D at $2.9B valuation

key_facts.fact: FuriosaAI announced a $620 million (KRW 820 billion) Series D round at a post-money valuation of about $2.9 billion.
key_facts.excerpt: FuriosaAI... today announced the completion of its $620 million (KRW 820 billion) Series D round, bringing its post-money valuation to approximately $2.9 billion.

key_facts.fact: South Korea's state-backed National Growth Fund contributed about $280 million (KRW 370 billion), the largest investor; international investors including Infinitum, Jericho Capital, QUDA Capital, Cisco Investments and NeoFort added $110 million.
key_facts.excerpt: The investment was led by South Korea's National Growth Fund, which injected $280 million of the total amount raised... Global investors including Cisco Investments, Abu Dhabi-based NeoFort Holdings, QUDA Capital Partners, Jericho Capital and Worldline Capital added another $110 million

key_facts.fact: The valuation is close to four times the $735 million FuriosaAI was reportedly worth after its July 2025 Series C bridge; the company earlier turned down an $800 million takeover offer from Meta.
key_facts.excerpt: The new valuation is close to four times the US$735 million FuriosaAI was reportedly worth after its US$125 million Series C bridge round in July 2025... the company had turned down a US$800 million takeover offer from Meta Platforms

key_facts.fact: FuriosaAI's RNGD inference accelerator is in mass production, with 20,000 cards this year and memory and fab capacity secured to more than double that in 2027; its third-generation chip is being developed with Broadcom and other partners.
key_facts.excerpt: Our RNGD inference accelerator is in mass production: we'll produce 20,000 cards this year, and we've secured the memory and fab capacity to more than double that in 2027... underway now with Broadcom and other partners

stories.headline: STMicro beats Q3 profit estimates, raises 2026 AI data-center revenue forecast to $1.3B

key_facts.fact: STMicroelectronics reported Q3 2026 net revenues of $3.76 billion, up 17.9% year over year, with non-GAAP operating income of $429 million.
key_facts.excerpt: ST reported third quarter net revenues of $3.76 billion, gross margin of 37.3%... (non-U.S. GAAP operating income of $429 million... On a year-over-year basis, Q3 net revenues increased 17.9%.

key_facts.fact: Operating income nearly doubled from a year earlier and beat the $400.5 million analysts expected; Q4 revenue guidance of $4.15 billion topped the $4.10 billion consensus.
key_facts.excerpt: The company's quarterly operating income excluding one-off charges was $429 million, nearly doubling from a year ago and beating the $400.5 million expected... It forecast fourth-quarter revenue of $4.15 billion... Analysts had expected $4.10 billion.

key_facts.fact: STMicro now expects about $1.3 billion in data-center revenue in 2026, up from a July forecast of more than $1 billion, driven mainly by silicon photonics chips, and reiterated a 2027 goal of well above $2 billion.
key_facts.excerpt: The Franco-Italian chipmaker now expects to book about $1.3 billion in data centre revenue in 2026, up from a July forecast of more than $1 billion. It reiterated the 2027 goal of well above $2 billion... driven mainly by STMicro's silicon photonics chips

key_facts.fact: The Q4 outlook implies full-year 2026 revenue of about $14.5 billion, up 22.8%; CEO Jean-Marc Chery said demand 'remains well above supply'.
key_facts.excerpt: The mid-point of this outlook translates into full year 2026 revenues of about $14.5 billion, representing a 22.8% year-over-year increase... In an environment where demand remains well above supply, we continue to expand capacity

stories.headline: Apple launches first touchscreen Mac: OLED MacBook Pro with M5 Pro/Max, $400 pricier

key_facts.fact: Apple introduced a MacBook Pro with a tandem-OLED 'PROLED XDR' display and Touch for the first time on a Mac, powered by M5 Pro and M5 Max chips with up to 128GB of unified memory and up to 16TB of storage.
key_facts.excerpt: The new MacBook Pro also introduces intuitive Touch capabilities on the Mac for the first time... Featuring M5 Pro and M5 Max, Apple's most powerful chips ever built for a pro laptop, along with up to 128GB of unified memory and now up to 16TB of blazing-fast storage

key_facts.fact: The display reaches up to 2,000 nits peak brightness with a 10,000,000:1 contrast ratio and 120Hz refresh; the Dynamic Island also comes to the Mac, and battery life is rated up to 24 hours.
key_facts.excerpt: up to 2000 nits peak HDR and SDR brightness, an industry-leading 10,000,000:1 contrast ratio... a 120Hz variable refresh rate... The Dynamic Island now comes to Mac... up to 24 hours of battery life

key_facts.fact: Pre-orders opened October 28 with availability from November 6; the 14-inch M5 Pro model starts at $2,899 and the 16-inch at $3,399, with M5 Max versions from $4,499 and $4,799.
key_facts.excerpt: The 14-inch MacBook Pro with PROLED XDR Display featuring M5 Pro starts at $2,899 (U.S.)... the 16-inch... starts at $3,399 (U.S.)... featuring M5 Max starts at $4,499 (U.S.)... 16-inch... M5 Max starts at $4,799

key_facts.fact: Entry prices are $400 above the previous non-touch models (about 16% for the base 14-inch), and a maxed-out 16-inch reaches $14,549, with the 16TB SSD option alone costing $7,000.
key_facts.excerpt: The $400 premium represents an increase of approximately 16% for the entry-level 14-inch M5 Pro configuration... the 16-inch model to reach $14,549... the new 16TB option costs $7,000.
